section_summary: This section finishes a report on Japanese local elections and by-elections, with a detailed Osaka election return and tables of results. It then covers the May 1949 demonstrations at the Tokyo Metropolitan Assembly and compares proposed public safety ordinances. The remaining papers discuss the political, economic and strategic future of occupied Japan, including a peace treaty, Japanese security and the scope of occupation control.

subfiles.title: Report on local general and by-elections in Japan
subfiles.about: Analyzes local election results and military government observations.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages compare party performance and candidate platforms in several prefectures, emphasizing independent candidates, Communist organizing and the costs of by-elections. Military government teams report on election conduct and local political trends. The report recommends plural voting and ending the requirement that officeholders resign before running for another office.

subfiles.title: Summary of Election: Kitakawachi District, Osaka Prefecture
subfiles.doc_type: military government letter and election return
subfiles.from: Frank Kowalski Jr., Osaka Military Government Team
subfiles.about: Reports the April 23, 1949 prefectural assembly election in Kitakawachi District.
subfiles.summary: The return compares voter registration, turnout and party votes with earlier elections. It lists four candidates, describes extensive voter publicity and their campaign issues, and reports no election violations.

subfiles.title: Local Election and By-Election Summary, January 1 to May 1, 1949
subfiles.about: Tabulates candidates and winners in local Japanese elections.
subfiles.summary: Tab B counts elections, seats, candidates and winning parties for governors, mayors, ward chiefs and local assemblies.

subfiles.title: Communist Planks on Odawara Municipal Administration
subfiles.from: Odawara Local Committee, Japan Communist Party
subfiles.about: Sets out the municipal program announced with Takechiyo Uchino's mayoral candidacy.
subfiles.summary: The translated platform presents eight general and 42 detailed proposals on taxation, municipal services, industry, farming, fishing, housing and education.

subfiles.title: Communist Vote Percentages in Selected Local Elections
subfiles.about: Compares local Communist vote shares with prefectural shares in the 1949 House election.
subfiles.summary: Tab D lists Communist vote percentages across selected gubernatorial, assembly and mayoral contests.

subfiles.title: Background of Riots at Tokyo Metropolitan Assembly, May 30–31, 1949
subfiles.about: Forwards Richard H. Lamb's memorandum on the Tokyo Assembly demonstrations.
subfiles.summary: The despatch summarizes competing model public safety ordinances and the apparent Communist effort to influence Tokyo's pending ordinance.

subfiles.title: Background of the Demonstrations at the Tokyo Metropolitan Assembly, May 30–31, 1949
subfiles.about: Examines the demonstrations and competing rules for public meetings.
subfiles.summary: Lamb contrasts a Government Section model ordinance covering parades with a more restrictive I Corps version covering standing meetings and making participants liable to arrest. He argues that Communist organizers likely sought to pressure the Tokyo Assembly, while cautioning that his account relies chiefly on one conversation and has not been independently confirmed.

subfiles.title: File of Papers on Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits and indexes papers on Japan's political, economic and strategic future.
subfiles.summary: Lists nine papers and recommends four for priority reading.

subfiles.title: Initial Report of Impressions Gathered on Brief Visit to Japan
subfiles.about: Records Bishop's impressions of occupied Japan after a brief visit.
subfiles.summary: Bishop observes material improvement alongside inadequate housing and transport, growing fatigue with occupation control and anxiety over Communist influence. He urges a prompt change in the occupation's character and movement toward a peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Conditions in Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses resistance to economic stabilization and proposes changes in occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum describes labor and political opposition to austerity, layoffs and proposed labor law changes, warning that worsening unrest could force reliance on occupation troops. It proposes faster implementation of NSC 13/2, revised occupation controls, economic announcements, wider Japanese foreign contacts and renewed support for an early peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Analysis of NSC 49: Current Strategic Evaluation of U.S. Security Needs in Japan
subfiles.about: Analyzes Joint Chiefs of Staff views on Japan's strategic value and a peace settlement.
subfiles.summary: The draft examines the Joint Chiefs' wish to keep Japan friendly, preserve access to bases and plan for Japanese self-defense. It questions whether continued occupation would better secure Japanese cooperation than a peace treaty and identifies political problems posed by future base rights.

subfiles.title: Extract on Naval Bases
subfiles.about: Quotes strategic guidance concerning Yokosuka naval facilities.
subfiles.summary: The extract discusses retaining use of Yokosuka facilities after a treaty.

subfiles.title: Obscurities in NSC 49 Requiring Clarification
subfiles.about: Lists questions about naval bases, U.S. forces and Japanese self-defense.
subfiles.summary: Seeks clarification of Yokosuka arrangements, future base rights, treaty safeguards and the timing of Japanese armed forces.

subfiles.title: Cover Memorandum on NSC 49 Analysis
subfiles.about: Forwards the draft NSC 49 analysis and questions requiring clarification.
subfiles.summary: Bishop recommends further discussion of the Joint Chiefs' views.

subfiles.title: Joint Chiefs' Position Compared with General MacArthur's Views
subfiles.about: Notes a possible conflict between Joint Chiefs' planning and MacArthur's opposition to rearming Japan before war.
subfiles.summary: Bishop suggests asking whether the Joint Chiefs coordinated their position with MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Political Situation in Japan
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese politics, occupation control, peace treaty opinion and security issues.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces postwar constitutional change and party politics through the January 1949 election, then examines Yoshida's government, Communist growth and opposition to occupation rule. It describes SCAP's role as a super-government and changing Japanese views of a peace treaty. Later sections consider political responsibility, police capacity, neutrality and defense. The document continues beyond page 442.
